overview: This entry is modern Greece, whose independence was recognized in 1830, rather than the ancient Greek city-states. The imported map label begins in 1878. The country later passed through monarchies, republics, war and dictatorship before the restoration of democracy in 1974 and the constitution of 1975.

periods.title: The kingdom
periods.summary: Greece was a constitutional monarchy during this part of its modern history.

periods.title: The second republic
periods.summary: The monarchy was abolished in 1924 and restored in 1935.

periods.title: Monarchy, dictatorship and war
periods.summary: Restored monarchy was followed by the Metaxas dictatorship, wartime occupation and further political upheaval.

periods.title: Military dictatorship
periods.summary: A military coup in 1967 began seven years of dictatorship.

periods.title: Democratic republic
periods.summary: Democracy returned in 1974. A referendum rejected monarchy, and a new constitution followed in 1975.

sections.title: A growing capital and the things beneath it

items.text: Athens rebuilt the Panathenaic Stadium for the first modern Olympic Games in 1896. The setting drew on an ancient stadium, but the new international event required modern reconstruction and organization. A famous old place became the stage for a new sporting institution.

After the upheavals of 1922, refugees arriving in Drama found temporary shelter in churches, mosques and houses. The Benaki Museum’s exhibition includes the Santirvan mosque’s use for housing. Objects carried by displaced families preserve memories of homes and communities left behind.

Athens needed much more water as its population grew, especially after the arrival of refugees in the 1920s. The Marathon dam and a new tunnel and distribution network expanded the city’s supply. Everyday washing, cooking and drinking depended on engineering far beyond the kitchen tap.

The Marathon dam was built between 1926 and 1929. Stone houses made for workers survive at the site, and the water museum preserves tools and film of construction. A large public work also meant a temporary community of people building, living and working together.

Building the Athens metro required extensive archaeological excavation. The metro company records tens of thousands of finds from the work. A transport project therefore also became a major investigation of the city’s earlier streets, buildings and buried objects.

Metro excavations uncovered wells, conduits and reservoirs beneath Athens, including deeply buried water structures. These remains show how earlier residents collected and moved water. Modern passengers can travel through a city whose underground layers preserve older answers to the same basic needs.

On Chios, mastic growers make small cuts in trees so resin can collect and harden into drops. Preparing the ground, tending trees, gathering resin and cleaning it form a seasonal cycle. A tiny piece of mastic represents many separate tasks rather than simply picking something from a branch.

UNESCO’s account describes mastic work as a family and community activity, with knowledge passed through practice and conversation. Cleaning the resin can bring people together to exchange stories. The social life around the work is part of the tradition alongside the finished product.

In 1976, Greece established demotic Greek, the language form closer to everyday speech, in education. Administration followed in 1977. The change affected the language children encountered in school after a long debate over the relationship between spoken Greek and more formal written forms.

Greece created its national health system, ESY, in 1983. The reform aimed to organize public healthcare on a common basis. Public and private services continued alongside one another, and later reviews identified uneven access and financing problems. Building a health system required more than passing its founding law.

A chef in Koroni describes using seasonal ingredients and giving leftovers another purpose: baked vegetables can go into a pie, while fish bones become stock. This is one restaurant’s account of contemporary practice. Yesterday’s ingredients can get a second act instead of a trip to the bin.

Modern Greek, constitution article 1: “Όλες οι εξουσίες πηγάζουν από το Λαό”. Translation: “All powers derive from the people.” This excerpt uses the demotic wording introduced in 1986, preserved in Parliament’s consolidated constitutional text. It should not be mistaken for the exact language of the original 1975 printing.

ending.text: Modern Greece continues as a republic. The 1974 referendum confirmed the rejection of monarchy after the military dictatorship collapsed. The state and its communities continued through the change of government. Its constitutional order was established in 1975 and subsequently revised.
